01.r: Links this scene to the one before.

02.r: Places the scene later than what went before.

04.r: Jesus goes out from the place of the previous scene.
04.n: The Greek leaves the subject in the verb; the BSB names Jesus.

05.r: Joins his going out to what he sees.

06.r: Jesus takes careful notice of Levi.
06.n: Not the common verb for 'see'. Abbott-Smith defines it as 'to behold, look upon, contemplate, view', and says that in the New Testament it is apparently always used in a literal, physical sense of careful looking. The ASV and YLT mark it with 'beheld'.

07.r: Levi's trade, given before his name.
07.n: Abbott-Smith cites this verse under his second sense: a subordinate who collected taxes or tolls in a particular district. This study renders it 'toll collector' throughout.

08.n: Literally 'by name', the noun 'name' in the dative, as the YLT has it.

09.n: Abbott-Smith lists the Levi of the call scene in Mark under 'Son of Alphaeus', with a cross-reference to Matthew. That the Levi here is the same man is the natural reading of the parallel scenes; it is an inference.

12.r: A particular booth, the one at that place.

13.r: The post where tolls were collected.
13.n: Abbott-Smith defines it as 'a custom house, tollhouse, place of toll', derived from τελώνης; he records it in this verse and the two parallel call scenes only. This study renders it 'toll booth'.

14.r: Joins what Jesus says to what he sees.

17.r: A call to come with Jesus as his disciple.
17.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'to accompany, follow' and a figurative sense 'of discipleship'. A present imperative, which the YLT brings out with 'Be following'.

18.r: Jesus himself, the one to be followed.
